newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Nov 4.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- South Africa and the U.S. have initialled a new bilateral tax treaty to replace the pact torn up by the Comprehensive Anti-Aparthied Act 10 years ago.
- Gold slumped to its lowest level in a month last week, fixing in London at $377.20 an ounce on Friday morning.
- The government's land redistribution programme has received a setback in the Free State where a group of prospective farmers lost their newly acquired land in a bad-debt auction last week.

- The ANC's national leadership has warned that failure to find a solution to the conflict between Free State premier Patrick Lekota and members of his government could lead to the dissolution of party's provincial executive committee.
- The rand meltdown which began in February has sent South African Airways SAA.CN losses soaring to 300 million rand for the six months to October 31.

- Foreign investors have been offloading large chunks of the 11 million South African Breweries shares traded since the middle of September, with selling pressure aggravating the recent weakness in the rand, local share dealers said.
- Labour minister Tito Mboweni defended the new Labour Relations Act against accusations that it would choke business to death and destroy jobs.
- Bateman Industrial Corp's proposed share incentive scheme has been slammed by the South African Shareholders' Association.
- The Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi will reopen a representative office in South Africa after a 10-year absence.
- The mothers of 10 Mamelodi youths lured to heir deaths by security police in 1986 have vowed never to forgive their sons' killers.
- A man was killed when police and supporters of the anti-drug group People Against Gangsterism and Drugs (Pagad) clashed at Cape Town's Waterfront.
